Option C (Amazon EMR) is for big data processing, not direct dashboarding. Option E (AWS Glue) is for ETL and data cataloging, not visualization.

text: Which AWS services are designed for building, training, and deploying machine learning models? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Rekognition","Amazon SageMaker","Amazon Comprehend","Amazon Lex","Amazon EMR"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon SageMaker) is a fully managed service that provides every developer and data scientist with the ability to build, train, and deploy machine learning models quickly. Option E (Amazon EMR) can be used for large-scale data processing, including machine learning workloads, by running frameworks like Apache Spark, which is often part of the ML pipeline. Options A (Amazon Rekognition), C (Amazon Comprehend), and D (Amazon Lex) are pre-trained AI services that provide specific ML functionalities (image/video analysis, natural language processing, chatbots) via API calls, but they are not for building, training, and deploying custom ML models from scratch.

text: A data analyst needs to run ad-hoc SQL queries directly on data stored in Amazon S3 without provisioning any servers. Which AWS analytics services would be suitable? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Redshift","Amazon Athena","AWS Glue","Amazon QuickSight","Amazon Kinesis"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon Athena) is a serverless query service that allows you to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL, without managing any infrastructure. Option C (AWS Glue) is a serverless data integration service that can also be used to run ETL jobs and catalog data, making it queryable by Athena, and it can execute Spark SQL queries on S3 data. Option A (Amazon Redshift) is a managed data warehouse that requires provisioning a cluster. Option D (Amazon QuickSight) is a business intelligence service for creating dashboards, not for running ad-hoc SQL queries on raw S3 data. Option E (Amazon Kinesis) is for real-time streaming data, not for ad-hoc SQL queries on static S3 data.

text: Which AWS services can be used to process and analyze real-time streaming data? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Redshift","Amazon Kinesis","AWS Glue","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon EMR"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon Kinesis) is a service specifically designed for real-time streaming data ingestion and processing, supporting various use cases like real-time analytics and application monitoring. Option E (Amazon EMR) can be configured to process real-time streaming data using frameworks like Apache Spark Streaming or Apache Flink. Option A (Amazon Redshift) is a data warehouse for analytical queries on large datasets, typically batch processing. Option C (AWS Glue) is primarily an ETL service for batch data processing and cataloging, though it has streaming ETL capabilities, Kinesis and EMR are more direct for real-time processing. Option D (Amazon DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database, not a streaming data processing service, though it can store streaming data.

text: Which AWS services allow you to create interactive dashboards and perform business intelligence (BI) analysis on your data? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Athena","Amazon QuickSight","AWS Glue","Amazon Redshift","Amazon EMR"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon QuickSight) is a scalable, serverless business intelligence (BI) service that allows you to create interactive dashboards and perform data analysis. Option D (Amazon Redshift) is a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse service that is often used as a data source for BI tools like QuickSight, and it allows for complex analytical queries. Option A (Amazon Athena) is a query service for S3 data, not primarily for dashboarding. Option C (AWS Glue) is an ETL service. Option E (Amazon EMR) is a big data processing service, not a BI dashboarding tool itself.

text: Which AWS services are designed for real-time data ingestion and processing, often used for IoT data or application logs? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Redshift","Amazon Kinesis","AWS Glue","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon EMR"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon Kinesis) is a fully managed service for real-time processing of large streams of data, ideal for IoT data, application logs, and clickstreams. Option E (Amazon EMR) can be used to process real-time streaming data using frameworks like Apache Spark Streaming or Apache Flink, making it suitable for complex real-time analytics on ingested data. Option A (Amazon Redshift) is a data warehouse for analytical queries, typically batch. Option C (AWS Glue) is primarily an ETL service for batch data. Option D (Amazon DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database, not a streaming ingestion or processing service.

text: Which AWS compute services are considered serverless, meaning AWS automatically provisions and manages the underlying infrastructure? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EC2","AWS Lambda","AWS Fargate","Amazon Lightsail","Amazon ECS"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service that runs your code in response to events without provisioning or managing servers. Option C (AWS Fargate) is a serverless compute engine for containers that works with Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS, eliminating the need to provision and manage servers. Option A (Amazon EC2) requires users to manage virtual servers. Option D (Amazon Lightsail) provides virtual private servers, but users still manage the OS. Option E (Amazon ECS) is a container orchestration service that can run on EC2 instances, which you manage, or with Fargate for serverless operation.

text: Which AWS services can automatically adjust compute capacity to meet demand, ensuring performance while optimizing costs? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)","Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling","AWS Lambda","Amazon S3","Amazon RDS"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling) automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances in your application based on defined policies, health checks, and schedules. Option C (AWS Lambda) is serverless and automatically scales its compute capacity based on the number of incoming requests or events, without any manual configuration. Option A (Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)) distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets but does not adjust compute capacity itself. Option D (Amazon S3) is object storage. Option E (Amazon RDS) is a managed database service that can scale storage and compute, but its primary function is not automatic compute capacity adjustment for general applications.

text: Which AWS services are designed to distribute incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, to improve application availability and fault tolerance? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Route 53","Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)","Amazon CloudFront","AWS Global Accelerator","AWS Direct Connect"]
explanation: Option B (Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)) automatically distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, in multiple Availability Zones. Option D (AWS Global Accelerator) improves the availability and performance of your applications by directing user traffic to the nearest healthy endpoint across the AWS global network. Option A (Amazon Route 53) is a DNS service. Option C (Amazon CloudFront) is a content delivery network. Option E (AWS Direct Connect) provides a dedicated network connection to AWS.

text: Which AWS compute services are designed for running event-driven code without provisioning or managing servers? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EC2","AWS Lambda","Amazon ECS","AWS Fargate","Amazon Lightsail"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Lambda) is the quintessential serverless compute service, executing code in response to events without managing servers. Option D (AWS Fargate) is a serverless compute engine for containers, meaning you don't manage the underlying EC2 instances that run your containers. Option A (Amazon EC2) requires managing virtual servers. Option C (Amazon ECS) is a container orchestration service that can use EC2 instances, which need management. Option E (Amazon Lightsail) provides simple virtual private servers, also requiring server management.

text: A web application experiences variable traffic throughout the day, requiring its compute capacity to scale automatically. Which AWS services can help achieve this elasticity and distribute incoming traffic? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EC2","AWS Auto Scaling","Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)","Amazon Lightsail","AWS Batch"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Auto Scaling) automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances (or other resources) in response to demand, ensuring capacity matches traffic. Option C (Elastic Load Balancing - ELB) distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, in multiple Availability Zones, ensuring high availability and fault tolerance. Option A (Amazon EC2) provides virtual servers but doesn't automatically scale or distribute traffic on its own. Option D (Amazon Lightsail) is for simple web applications and virtual private servers, with less granular scaling options than Auto Scaling. Option E (AWS Batch) is for running batch computing workloads, not for handling variable web traffic.

text: Which Amazon EC2 pricing options are suitable for workloads with predictable usage patterns that can commit to a 1-year or 3-year term, offering significant cost savings? (Select TWO.)
options: ["On-Demand Instances","Reserved Instances","Spot Instances","Savings Plans","Dedicated Hosts"]
explanation: Option B (Reserved Instances) offer a significant discount (up to 75%) compared to On-Demand pricing in exchange for committing to a 1-year or 3-year term for specific instance types in a Region. Option D (Savings Plans) offer even greater flexibility than RIs, providing lower prices (up to 72% savings) on EC2 usage (and Fargate/Lambda) in exchange for a commitment to a consistent amount of compute usage (measured in $/hour) for a 1-year or 3-year term. Option A (On-Demand Instances) are for flexible, short-term, or unpredictable workloads. Option C (Spot Instances) are for fault-tolerant workloads that can tolerate interruptions, offering up to 90% savings. Option E (Dedicated Hosts) provide physical EC2 servers for your exclusive use, primarily for licensing or regulatory requirements, not primarily for cost savings on predictable usage.

text: A company needs to host a simple web application with a fixed monthly cost and minimal management. Which AWS compute services are designed for this type of straightforward deployment? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EC2 (with Auto Scaling)","AWS Lambda","Amazon Lightsail","Amazon ECS (with Fargate)","AWS Elastic Beanstalk"]
explanation: Option C (Amazon Lightsail) is designed for simple web applications, offering virtual private servers (VPS), databases, and more with a fixed monthly price and easy management. Option E (AWS Elastic Beanstalk) is a Platform as a Service (PaaS) that simplifies deploying and scaling web applications, abstracting away much of the underlying infrastructure management, making it suitable for minimal management. Option A (Amazon EC2 with Auto Scaling) offers more flexibility but requires more configuration and management than Lightsail or Elastic Beanstalk. Option B (AWS Lambda) is serverless and event-driven, not typically for a 'simple web application' with a fixed monthly cost model, as it's pay-per-invocation. Option D (Amazon ECS with Fargate) is for containerized applications, offering serverless containers, but might be overkill for a 'simple' web app compared to Lightsail or Elastic Beanstalk.

text: Which AWS compute services are considered serverless, meaning you don't need to provision or manage servers? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EC2","AWS Lambda","Amazon ECS","AWS Fargate","Amazon Lightsail"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service that runs code in response to events without provisioning or managing servers. Option D (AWS Fargate) is a serverless compute engine for Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS that allows you to run containers without having to provision, manage, or scale clusters of virtual machines. Option A (Amazon EC2) requires you to provision and manage virtual servers. Option C (Amazon ECS) is a container orchestration service that typically runs on EC2 instances, though it can use Fargate. Option E (Amazon Lightsail) provides virtual private servers, which still require server management.

text: A company needs to run a web application that experiences unpredictable traffic spikes. Which AWS compute features help automatically adjust capacity to meet demand? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances","Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)","Amazon EC2 Spot Instances","AWS Auto Scaling","Amazon Lightsail"]
explanation: Option B (Elastic Load Balancing - ELB) distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, ensuring that no single instance is overwhelmed. Option D (AWS Auto Scaling) automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances in response to changing demand, adding instances during spikes and removing them during lulls. Option A (Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances) are a pricing model for predictable workloads, not for automatic capacity adjustment. Option C (Amazon EC2 Spot Instances) are for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads where interruptions are acceptable, not primarily for handling unpredictable traffic spikes without manual intervention. Option E (Amazon Lightsail) is for simple web applications and virtual private servers, without built-in automatic scaling capabilities like Auto Scaling.

text: A company wants to run containerized applications and prefers a managed service that handles the underlying infrastructure. Which AWS services support container orchestration? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Lambda","Amazon EC2","Amazon ECS","Amazon EKS","Amazon Lightsail"]
explanation: Option C (Amazon ECS - Elastic Container Service) and Option D (Amazon EKS - Elastic Kubernetes Service) are AWS's primary container orchestration services. ECS is a highly scalable, high-performance container orchestration service that supports Docker containers. EKS is a managed service that makes it easy to run Kubernetes on AWS without needing to install, operate, and maintain your own Kubernetes control plane. Option A (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service for functions, not containers. Option B (Amazon EC2) provides virtual servers, which can host containers but require manual orchestration. Option E (Amazon Lightsail) offers virtual private servers and simple container deployments, but not full-fledged container orchestration.

text: Which of the following are benefits of using AWS Lambda for compute workloads? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Full control over the underlying operating system","Automatic scaling based on demand","Pay only for the compute time consumed","Ability to run long-running, stateful applications","Fixed monthly cost for predictable usage"]
explanation: Option B (Automatic scaling based on demand) is a key benefit of AWS Lambda, as it automatically scales out to handle incoming requests without any configuration. Option C (Pay only for the compute time consumed) is also a core advantage, as Lambda charges based on the number of requests and the duration of execution, not for idle time. Option A (Full control over the underlying operating system) is incorrect; Lambda is serverless, abstracting away the OS. Option D (Ability to run long-running, stateful applications) is generally incorrect; Lambda functions are stateless and have a maximum execution duration. Option E (Fixed monthly cost for predictable usage) is incorrect; Lambda's cost is variable based on actual usage, though it can be predictable for consistent workloads, it's not a fixed monthly cost model.

text: Which AWS compute services allow you to run code without provisioning or managing servers? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EC2","AWS Lambda","Amazon ECS","AWS Fargate","Amazon Lightsail"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service that runs code in response to events without provisioning or managing servers. text: A company needs to host a simple web application that requires a virtual private server (VPS) with predictable pricing. Which AWS services are suitable for this use case? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EC2","AWS Lambda","Amazon Lightsail","AWS Elastic Beanstalk","AWS Fargate"]
explanation: Option A (Amazon EC2) provides virtual servers (instances) that can host web applications, and with Reserved Instances or Savings Plans, pricing can be predictable. Option C (Amazon Lightsail) is specifically designed for simple web applications and virtual private servers, offering bundled pricing plans for ease of use and predictability. Option B (AWS Lambda) is serverless compute for event-driven functions, not a VPS. Option D (AWS Elastic Beanstalk) is a PaaS that abstracts servers, but Lightsail is simpler for a basic VPS. Option E (AWS Fargate) is a serverless compute engine for containers, not a VPS.

text: Which AWS services can distribute incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, to improve availability and fault tolerance? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Route 53","Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)","Amazon CloudFront","AWS Global Accelerator","AWS Auto Scaling"]
explanation: Option B (Elastic Load Balancing - ELB) automatically distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, in multiple Availability Zones, enhancing the fault tolerance of your applications. Option D (AWS Global Accelerator) improves the availability and performance of your applications by directing user traffic to optimal endpoints over the AWS global network, which includes distributing traffic across multiple Regions or endpoints within a Region. Option E (AWS Auto Scaling) adjusts the number of instances, but ELB and Global Accelerator are responsible for traffic distribution.

text: Which Amazon EC2 instance types are best suited for workloads that require high CPU performance and benefit from extensive processing power? (Select TWO.)
options: ["General Purpose (e.g., M-series)","Compute Optimized (e.g., C-series)","Memory Optimized (e.g., R-series)","Storage Optimized (e.g., I-series)","Accelerated Computing (e.g., P-series)"]
explanation: Option B (Compute Optimized - e.g., C-series) instances are designed for compute-intensive applications that benefit from high-performance processors. Option E (Accelerated Computing - e.g., P-series) instances use hardware accelerators, or co-processors, to perform functions such as floating-point number calculations, graphics processing, or data pattern matching more efficiently than software running on CPUs, making them ideal for high CPU performance tasks. Option A (General Purpose - e.g., M-series) instances provide a balance of compute, memory, and networking resources. Option C (Memory Optimized - e.g., R-series) instances are designed for memory-intensive applications. Option D (Storage Optimized - e.g., I-series) instances are designed for workloads that require high, sequential read and write access to very large datasets on local storage.

text: Which AWS services can be used to manage and orchestrate containerized applications? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Lambda","Amazon EC2","Amazon ECS","Amazon EKS","Amazon Lightsail"]
explanation: Option C (Amazon ECS - Elastic Container Service) is a highly scalable, high-performance container orchestration service that supports Docker containers. Option D (Amazon EKS - Elastic Kubernetes Service) is a managed service that makes it easy to run Kubernetes on AWS. Both are designed for managing and orchestrating containerized applications. text: Which AWS database services are fully managed relational databases? (Select TWO.)

text: A company needs a highly scalable, fully managed NoSQL database for an application with variable access patterns and high throughput requirements. Which AWS services are suitable? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon RDS","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon Aurora","Amazon DocumentDB","Amazon Redshift"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon DynamoDB) is a fully managed NoSQL (key-value and document) database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale, making it ideal for high throughput and variable access patterns. Option D (Amazon DocumentDB) is a fully managed native JSON document database that supports MongoDB workloads, suitable for document-oriented NoSQL needs. Option A (Amazon RDS) and Option C (Amazon Aurora) are relational databases. Option E (Amazon Redshift) is a data warehouse for analytics, not an operational NoSQL database.

text: Which AWS services provide in-memory caching to improve application performance and reduce the load on databases? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon S3","Amazon ElastiCache","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon MemoryDB for Redis","Amazon RDS"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon ElastiCache) is a fully managed in-memory caching service that supports Redis and Memcached, significantly speeding up data retrieval. Option D (Amazon MemoryDB for Redis) is a durable, in-memory database service that delivers ultra-fast performance with multi-AZ durability and security. Option A (Amazon S3) is object storage. Option C (Amazon DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database. Option E (Amazon RDS) is a relational database service.

text: For analytical workloads requiring complex queries over petabytes of data, which AWS services are purpose-built for data warehousing and analytics? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon RDS","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon Redshift","Amazon Aurora","Amazon Athena"]
explanation: Option C (Amazon Redshift) is a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse service optimized for analytical workloads and complex queries. Option E (Amazon Athena) is a serverless query service that allows you to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL, suitable for ad-hoc analytics on large datasets. Option A (Amazon RDS) and Option D (Amazon Aurora) are relational databases optimized for transactional workloads. Option B (Amazon DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database for operational workloads.

text: To offload read traffic from a primary relational database and improve application responsiveness, which AWS services can be implemented? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon ElastiCache","Amazon Aurora Read Replicas","Amazon Redshift","Amazon S3"]

text: Which AWS database services are categorized as fully managed relational databases? (Select TWO.)

explanation: Option B (Amazon RDS) is a managed relational database service that supports various database engines like MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and SQL Server. text: A company needs a highly scalable, fully managed NoSQL database for an application with unpredictable, high-volume traffic patterns. Which AWS database services would be suitable? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon RDS","Amazon Aurora","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon Redshift","Amazon DocumentDB"]

Option E (Amazon DocumentDB) is a fully managed native JSON document database that supports MongoDB workloads, offering scalability for document-oriented NoSQL use cases. Option A (Amazon RDS) and Option B (Amazon Aurora) are relational databases, which are not ideal for highly variable NoSQL data patterns. Option D (Amazon Redshift) is a data warehouse, optimized for analytical queries, not transactional NoSQL workloads.

text: Which AWS database services are optimized for analytical workloads and data warehousing at scale? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon RDS","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon Redshift","Amazon Aurora","Amazon Athena"]
explanation: Option C (Amazon Redshift) is a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehousing service specifically designed for analytical queries on large datasets. Option E (Amazon Athena) is a serverless query service that allows you to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL, making it suitable for ad-hoc analytical queries on data lakes. Option A (Amazon RDS) and Option D (Amazon Aurora) are relational databases optimized for online transaction processing (OLTP). Option B (Amazon DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database optimized for high-performance transactional workloads.

text: A developer needs to improve the read performance of a database and offload read traffic from the primary database instance. Which AWS services can help achieve this? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon ElastiCache","Amazon Redshift","Amazon RDS Read Replicas","Amazon DocumentDB"]

Option E (Amazon DocumentDB) is a NoSQL document database, not a read-offload solution for relational databases.

text: Which AWS database services are suitable for use cases requiring in-memory data stores for sub-millisecond latency? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon RDS","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon ElastiCache","Amazon Redshift","Amazon MemoryDB for Redis"]
explanation: Option C (Amazon ElastiCache) is a fully managed in-memory caching service that supports Redis and Memcached, providing sub-millisecond latency for frequently accessed data. Option E (Amazon MemoryDB for Redis) is a Redis-compatible, durable, in-memory database service that delivers ultra-fast performance. Option A (Amazon RDS) is a relational database, not designed for in-memory caching. Option B (Amazon DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database, offering single-digit millisecond performance, but not typically sub-millisecond like in-memory stores. Option D (Amazon Redshift) is a data warehouse for analytical queries, not for low-latency transactional or caching use cases.

text: Which AWS database services are categorized as relational databases? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon RDS","Amazon Redshift","Amazon Aurora","Amazon ElastiCache"]

Option C (Amazon Redshift) is a data warehouse for analytics, not a transactional relational database. Option E (Amazon ElastiCache) is an in-memory caching service.

text: A company needs a highly scalable, fully managed NoSQL database that can handle millions of requests per second with single-digit millisecond latency. Which AWS database services would meet this requirement? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon RDS","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon Aurora","Amazon Redshift","Amazon ElastiCache"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon DynamoDB) is a fully managed NoSQL database service that provides fast and predictable performance with seamless scalability, capable of handling millions of requests per second with single-digit millisecond latency. Option A (Amazon RDS) and Option C (Amazon Aurora) are relational databases, which are not typically designed for the same scale and low-latency characteristics as DynamoDB for NoSQL workloads. Option D (Amazon Redshift) is a data warehouse for analytics, not a transactional database for high-volume, low-latency operational workloads.

text: Which AWS database services are suitable for analytical workloads and data warehousing at scale? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon RDS","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon Redshift","Amazon Aurora","Amazon Athena"]
explanation: Option C (Amazon Redshift) is a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse service specifically designed for analytical workloads. Option E (Amazon Athena) is a serverless query service that allows you to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL, making it suitable for ad-hoc analytical queries on large datasets. Option A (Amazon RDS) and Option D (Amazon Aurora) are relational databases optimized for online transaction processing (OLTP), not large-scale analytics. Option B (Amazon DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database for operational workloads, not primarily for complex analytical queries across vast datasets.

text: A company is migrating its on-premises relational database to AWS and wants to minimize operational overhead for tasks like backups, patching, and scaling. Which AWS database services offer managed relational database capabilities? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EC2 with self-managed database","Amazon RDS","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon Aurora","Amazon ElastiCache"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon RDS - Relational Database Service) and Option D (Amazon Aurora) are fully managed relational database services. They automate administrative tasks like backups, patching, scaling, and replication, significantly reducing operational overhead. Option A (Amazon EC2 with self-managed database) would require the customer to manually manage all database operations, increasing overhead. Option C (Amazon DynamoDB) is a managed NoSQL database, not relational. Option E (Amazon ElastiCache) is an in-memory caching service, not a primary relational database.

text: Which AWS database services are fully managed and support a relational data model? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon RDS","Amazon Redshift","Amazon Aurora","Amazon Neptune"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon RDS - Relational Database Service) is a fully managed service that makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale a relational database in the cloud. Option D (Amazon Aurora) is a MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database built for the cloud, combining the performance and availability of high-end commercial databases with the simplicity and cost-effectiveness of open-source databases. Option A (Amazon DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database. Option C (Amazon Redshift) is a data warehouse, not a transactional relational database. Option E (Amazon Neptune) is a graph database.

text: Which AWS services are suitable for storing frequently accessed, non-relational data that requires high throughput and low latency? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon RDS","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon Aurora","Amazon ElastiCache","Amazon Redshift"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon DynamoDB) is a fully managed NoSQL database service that provides fast and predictable performance with seamless scalability for non-relational data, offering single-digit millisecond latency at any scale. Option D (Amazon ElastiCache) provides in-memory caching for microsecond-latency data retrieval, which is ideal for frequently accessed data to offload the primary database and improve application performance. Option A (Amazon RDS) and Option C (Amazon Aurora) are relational databases. Option E (Amazon Redshift) is a data warehouse for analytics, not for high-throughput, low-latency operational access to individual non-relational items.

text: Which AWS networking components are used to isolate and control traffic within a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Internet Gateways","Security Groups","Network Access Control Lists (ACLs)","NAT Gateways","VPC Endpoints"]
explanation: Option B (Security Groups) act as a virtual firewall for EC2 instances, controlling inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level. Option C (Network Access Control Lists (ACLs)) are stateless firewalls that control traffic at the subnet level. Both are crucial for network isolation and access control within a VPC. Option A (Internet Gateways) enable internet connectivity for a VPC. Option D (NAT Gateways) allow instances in private subnets to connect to the internet or other AWS services, but not for isolation within the VPC. Option E (VPC Endpoints) enable private connections to AWS services.

text: Which AWS services are primarily used for managing domain names and routing internet traffic to AWS resources? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon CloudFront","Amazon Route 53","Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)","AWS Global Accelerator","AWS VPN"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon Route 53) is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service that can register domain names and route traffic to various AWS resources. Option D (AWS Global Accelerator) improves the availability and performance of your applications by directing user traffic to the nearest healthy endpoint across the AWS global network, often working in conjunction with DNS. Option A (Amazon CloudFront) is a content delivery network. Option C (Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)) distributes traffic to targets within a Region. Option E (AWS VPN) provides encrypted connections to AWS.

text: A company wants to improve the performance and reduce latency for users accessing their web application globally. Which AWS services can help deliver content closer to users? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon VPC","Amazon CloudFront","AWS Global Accelerator","AWS Direct Connect","Amazon Route 53"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon CloudFront) is a content delivery network (CDN) service that securely delivers data, videos, applications, and APIs to customers globally with low latency. Option C (AWS Global Accelerator) improves the availability and performance of your applications by directing user traffic to the nearest healthy endpoint across the AWS global network. Option A (Amazon VPC) provides network isolation. Option D (AWS Direct Connect) provides a dedicated network connection to AWS. Option E (Amazon Route 53) is a DNS service.

text: Which AWS networking services enable secure and private connectivity between your on-premises network and your AWS Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon CloudFront","AWS Direct Connect","AWS VPN","Amazon Route 53","Internet Gateway"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Direct Connect) provides a dedicated, private network connection from your premises to AWS, offering consistent network performance. Option C (AWS VPN) establishes an encrypted connection over the public internet between your on-premises network and your AWS VPC. Option A (Amazon CloudFront) is a content delivery network. Option D (Amazon Route 53) is a DNS web service. Option E (Internet Gateway) connects a VPC to the internet, not securely to an on-premises network.

text: Which AWS networking components act as firewalls to control traffic to and from resources within a VPC? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Route Tables","Security Groups","Network Access Control Lists (ACLs)","Internet Gateways","NAT Gateways"]
explanation: Option B (Security Groups) are stateful firewalls that operate at the instance level, controlling traffic for specific EC2 instances. Option C (Network Access Control Lists (ACLs)) are stateless firewalls that operate at the subnet level, controlling traffic for entire subnets. Both are critical for implementing network security within a VPC. Option A (Route Tables) determine where network traffic from your subnets is directed. Option D (Internet Gateways) allow internet access for a VPC. Option E (NAT Gateways) enable private subnet instances to initiate outbound connections to the internet.

text: Which AWS networking components are used to control inbound and outbound traffic for EC2 instances at the instance level and subnet level, respectively? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Internet Gateways","Security Groups","NAT Gateways","Network Access Control Lists (ACLs)","Route Tables"]
explanation: Option B (Security Groups) act as a virtual firewall for EC2 instances, controlling inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level. They are stateful. Option D (Network Access Control Lists - ACLs) act as a firewall for subnets, controlling inbound and outbound traffic at the subnet level. They are stateless, requiring separate rules for inbound and outbound traffic. Option A (Internet Gateways) enable communication between your VPC and the internet. Option C (NAT Gateways) allow instances in private subnets to connect to the internet or other AWS services, but prevent inbound connections from the internet. Option E (Route Tables) contain rules that determine where network traffic from your subnets is directed.

text: A company needs to ensure that its application servers in a private subnet can initiate outbound connections to the internet for updates, but remain inaccessible from the internet. Which AWS networking components are required for this setup? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Internet Gateway","Public Subnet","NAT Gateway","VPC Peering","Direct Connect"]
explanation: Option A (Internet Gateway) is required to allow communication between your VPC and the internet. Without it, no internet access is possible. Option C (NAT Gateway) allows instances in a private subnet to connect to the internet (via the Internet Gateway in a public subnet) but prevents the internet from initiating connections to those instances. Option B (Public Subnet) is where the NAT Gateway would reside, but it's not directly enabling the private subnet's outbound access. Option D (VPC Peering) connects two VPCs, not a private subnet to the internet. Option E (Direct Connect) provides a dedicated connection to AWS from on-premises, not for private subnets to access the internet.

text: Which AWS services are used for managing DNS and providing content delivery network (CDN) capabilities to improve application performance and availability? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon VPC","Amazon Route 53","AWS Direct Connect","Amazon CloudFront","AWS VPN"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon Route 53) is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service, used for domain registration and routing traffic. Option D (Amazon CloudFront) is a fast content delivery network (CDN) service that securely delivers data, videos, applications, and APIs to customers globally with low latency. Option A (Amazon VPC) is for creating isolated network environments. Option C (AWS Direct Connect) provides a dedicated network connection to AWS from on-premises. Option E (AWS VPN) establishes encrypted connections over the internet. Neither VPC, Direct Connect, nor VPN are for DNS or CDN.

text: Which AWS networking services allow for connecting multiple Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) together or connecting VPCs to on-premises networks through a central hub? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Internet Gateway","VPC Peering","NAT Gateway","AWS Transit Gateway","Amazon Route 53"]
explanation: Option B (VPC Peering) allows you to connect two VPCs directly, enabling instances in either VPC to communicate with each other as if they are within the same network. Option D (AWS Transit Gateway) acts as a network transit hub, allowing you to connect thousands of VPCs and on-premises networks through a central gateway, simplifying network management. Option A (Internet Gateway) connects a VPC to the internet. Option C (NAT Gateway) enables instances in a private subnet to access the internet. Option E (Amazon Route 53) is a DNS service, not for direct VPC-to-VPC or VPC-to-on-premises connectivity.

text: Which AWS networking components are used to control inbound and outbound traffic for EC2 instances? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Internet Gateway","Security Groups","NAT Gateway","Network Access Control Lists (NACLs)","VPC Peering"]
explanation: Option B (Security Groups) and Option D (Network Access Control Lists - NACLs) are used to control traffic to and from EC2 instances. Security Groups act as a virtual firewall for instances, controlling traffic at the instance level and are stateful. NACLs operate at the subnet level, acting as a stateless firewall for all traffic entering or leaving the subnet. Option A (Internet Gateway) allows instances in a public subnet to connect to the internet. Option C (NAT Gateway) allows instances in a private subnet to initiate outbound connections to the internet. Option E (VPC Peering) connects two VPCs, enabling communication between them.

text: A company needs to host a public-facing web application in a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Which components are necessary to allow internet users to access the application? (Select TWO.)
options: ["NAT Gateway","Internet Gateway","Private Subnet","Public Subnet","VPC Peering"]
explanation: Option B (Internet Gateway) is essential as it allows communication between instances in your VPC and the internet. Option D (Public Subnet) is where the public-facing resources, such as web servers, should be placed to be directly accessible from the internet via the Internet Gateway. Option A (NAT Gateway) is used for instances in private subnets to initiate outbound internet connections, not for inbound public access. Option C (Private Subnet) is for resources that should not be directly accessible from the internet. Option E (VPC Peering) connects two VPCs, not for internet access.

text: Which AWS networking services can be used to establish secure connections between an on-premises data center and an AWS VPC? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon CloudFront","AWS Direct Connect","Amazon Route 53","AWS VPN","VPC Peering"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Direct Connect) provides a dedicated, private network connection from your premises to AWS, offering consistent network performance. Option D (AWS VPN) establishes an encrypted connection over the public internet between your on-premises network and your AWS VPC. Option A (Amazon CloudFront) is a Content Delivery Network (CDN). Option C (Amazon Route 53) is a DNS web service. Option E (VPC Peering) connects two VPCs within AWS, not an on-premises network.

text: Which AWS services are primarily used for managing DNS and content delivery to improve global performance and availability? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon VPC","Amazon Route 53","Amazon CloudFront","AWS Direct Connect","Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon Route 53) is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service that can route users to applications globally. Option C (Amazon CloudFront) is a fast content delivery network (CDN) service that securely delivers data, videos, applications, and APIs to customers globally with low latency. Option A (Amazon VPC) is for creating isolated network environments. Option D (AWS Direct Connect) provides a dedicated network connection to AWS. Option E (Elastic Load Balancing) distributes traffic within a Region, not primarily for global content delivery or DNS management.

text: A company wants to protect its backend database servers by placing them in a private subnet. Which networking components are needed to allow these servers to download software updates from the internet while remaining inaccessible from the internet? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Internet Gateway","Public Subnet","NAT Gateway","Route Table with a route to the NAT Gateway","VPC Endpoint"]
explanation: Option C (NAT Gateway) allows instances in a private subnet to connect to the internet or other AWS services, but prevents the internet from initiating connections to those instances. Option D (Route Table with a route to the NAT Gateway) is necessary to direct traffic from the private subnet to the NAT Gateway for outbound internet access. Option A (Internet Gateway) is for public inbound and outbound access, which would expose the database. Option B (Public Subnet) would expose the database directly to the internet. Option E (VPC Endpoint) allows private connectivity to AWS services without traversing the internet, which is different from general internet access for software updates.

text: Which AWS networking components are used to define the network boundaries and routing within a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Security Groups","Subnets","Internet Gateway","Route Tables","Network ACLs"]
explanation: Option B (Subnets) are logical subdivisions of a VPC, allowing you to segment your network for security and organizational purposes. Option D (Route Tables) contain a set of rules, called routes, that determine where network traffic from your subnet or gateway is directed. Option A (Security Groups) and Option E (Network ACLs) are for controlling traffic flow, not defining network boundaries or routing. Option C (Internet Gateway) connects a VPC to the internet.

text: Which AWS networking services help improve the performance and availability of applications by routing traffic to optimal endpoints? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon VPC","Amazon Route 53","Amazon CloudFront","AWS Direct Connect","AWS Global Accelerator"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon Route 53) is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service that can route users to optimal application endpoints based on various routing policies (e.g., latency-based, weighted, failover). Option E (AWS Global Accelerator) improves the availability and performance of your applications with local or global users by directing user traffic to optimal endpoints over the AWS global network. Option A (Amazon VPC) defines your private network. Option C (Amazon CloudFront) is a CDN for content delivery, not primarily for routing application traffic to optimal endpoints. Option D (AWS Direct Connect) provides a dedicated network connection, but doesn't handle traffic routing optimization at the application level.

text: Which Amazon S3 features help protect data from accidental deletion and manage storage costs over time? (Select TWO.)
options: ["S3 Transfer Acceleration","S3 Versioning","S3 Lifecycle Policies","S3 Cross-Region Replication","S3 Object Lock"]
explanation: Option B (S3 Versioning) keeps multiple versions of an object in the same bucket, protecting against accidental overwrites or deletions. Option C (S3 Lifecycle Policies) define rules to automatically transition objects to different storage classes or expire them after a certain period, helping manage storage costs. Option A (S3 Transfer Acceleration) speeds up data transfers. Option D (S3 Cross-Region Replication) copies objects across Regions for disaster recovery. Option E (S3 Object Lock) provides WORM (Write Once Read Many) protection for regulatory compliance, which is for data integrity, not primarily cost management or accidental deletion protection in the general sense.

text: A media company needs shared file storage that can be accessed concurrently by thousands of Amazon EC2 instances for video processing. Which AWS services are suitable? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EBS","Amazon EFS","Amazon S3","Amazon FSx for Lustre","AWS Storage Gateway"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon EFS) provides scalable, elastic, shared file storage that can be mounted by thousands of EC2 instances concurrently using the NFS protocol. Option D (Amazon FSx for Lustre) provides a high-performance file system optimized for compute-intensive workloads like video processing, also allowing multiple instances to access shared data. Option A (Amazon EBS) provides block storage for a single EC2 instance (with Multi-Attach for specific volume types, but EFS/FSx are better for general shared access). Option C (Amazon S3) is object storage, not a file system. Option E (AWS Storage Gateway) is for hybrid cloud storage, not primary shared file storage for EC2 instances.

text: For migrating petabytes of data from an on-premises data center to AWS when internet connectivity is limited or too slow, which AWS services can be utilized? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Direct Connect","AWS Snowball","AWS DataSync","AWS Snowmobile","AWS VPN"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Snowball) is a petabyte-scale data transport solution that uses secure appliances to transfer large amounts of data into and out of AWS. Option D (AWS Snowmobile) is an exabyte-scale data transfer service used to move extremely large amounts of data to AWS. Both are part of the AWS Snow Family designed for offline data migration. Option A (AWS Direct Connect) and Option E (AWS VPN) are for online network connectivity, not offline data transfer. Option C (AWS DataSync) is an online data transfer service for moving data between on-premises storage and AWS storage services.

text: Which Amazon S3 storage classes are designed for frequently accessed data, offering high durability and availability? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive","Amazon S3 Standard","Amazon S3 One Zone-IA","Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering","Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon S3 Standard) is for general-purpose storage of frequently accessed data, offering high durability and availability. Option D (Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering) automatically moves data between two access tiers (frequent and infrequent) based on changing access patterns, making it suitable for data with unknown or changing access, while still providing high durability and availability for frequently accessed data. Option A (Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive) and Option E (Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval) are for archival data with long retrieval times. Option C (Amazon S3 One Zone-IA) is for infrequently accessed data that can be recreated, offering lower durability as it stores data in a single Availability Zone.

text: A company needs shared file storage that can be mounted by thousands of EC2 instances simultaneously and requires persistent block storage for individual EC2 instances. Which AWS storage services meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon S3","Amazon EBS","Amazon EFS","AWS Storage Gateway","AWS Snowball"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon EBS) provides persistent block storage volumes for use with individual Amazon EC2 instances. Option C (Amazon EFS) provides scalable, elastic file storage that can be mounted by thousands of EC2 instances simultaneously, supporting shared file access. Option A (Amazon S3) is object storage, not block or file storage that can be mounted by instances. Option D (AWS Storage Gateway) is for hybrid cloud storage, connecting on-premises software appliances to cloud storage. Option E (AWS Snowball) is for large-scale data transfer, not for active, mounted storage.

text: Which Amazon S3 features help protect objects from accidental deletion or overwrites and automatically transition objects to more cost-effective storage classes? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Static website hosting","Versioning","Object-level access controls","Lifecycle policies","Cross-Region Replication"]
explanation: Option B (Versioning) keeps multiple versions of an object in the same S3 bucket, protecting against accidental overwrites and deletions. Option D (Lifecycle policies) define rules to automatically transition objects to different S3 storage classes (e.g., from Standard to Standard-IA or Glacier) or expire them after a certain period, optimizing costs. Option A (Static website hosting) is a feature for hosting websites, not for data protection or cost optimization. Option C (Object-level access controls) manage permissions but don't prevent accidental deletion of existing versions. Option E (Cross-Region Replication) copies objects to another Region for disaster recovery, but doesn't manage versions or lifecycle within a single bucket.

text: A company needs to transfer petabytes of data from its on-premises data center to AWS, and also requires a hybrid cloud storage solution for infrequently accessed on-premises data. Which AWS services can address these requirements? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon S3","AWS Snow Family","Amazon EBS","AWS Storage Gateway","Amazon EFS"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Snow Family) provides physical devices (Snowcone, Snowball, Snowmobile) for securely transferring large amounts of data (petabytes to exabytes) into and out of AWS, which is ideal for petabyte-scale migrations. Option D (AWS Storage Gateway) is a hybrid cloud storage service that connects an on-premises software appliance with cloud-based storage, enabling on-premises applications to use AWS cloud storage for backup, archiving, and disaster recovery, including for infrequently accessed data. Option A (Amazon S3) is the destination for the data but not the transfer mechanism for petabytes over the internet. Option C (Amazon EBS) provides block storage for EC2 instances. Option E (Amazon EFS) provides shared file storage for EC2 instances.

text: Which Amazon S3 storage classes are designed for data that is accessed infrequently but requires rapid retrieval when needed? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon S3 Standard","Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering","Amazon S3 Standard-IA","Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval","Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive"]
explanation: Option C (Amazon S3 Standard-IA - Infrequent Access) is designed for data that is accessed less frequently but requires rapid access when needed, offering lower storage costs than S3 Standard. Option D (Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval) is also for long-lived, rarely accessed data that requires immediate retrieval, offering a balance between cost and speed. Option A (Amazon S3 Standard) is for frequently accessed data. Option B (Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering) automatically moves data between access tiers based on access patterns, but Standard-IA and Glacier Instant Retrieval are explicit choices for infrequent access. Option E (Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive) is for long-term archives with retrieval times measured in hours.

text: A company needs to store large files that will be accessed by multiple EC2 instances simultaneously using a shared file system. Which AWS storage services would be suitable? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon S3","Amazon EBS","Amazon EFS","Amazon FSx for Windows File Server","AWS Storage Gateway"]
explanation: Option C (Amazon EFS - Elastic File System) provides a scalable, shared file system that can be mounted by multiple EC2 instances concurrently using the NFS protocol. Option D (Amazon FSx for Windows File Server) provides fully managed native Microsoft Windows file systems, which can also be accessed by multiple EC2 instances simultaneously. Option A (Amazon S3) is object storage, not a file system that can be mounted by instances. Option B (Amazon EBS - Elastic Block Store) provides block storage volumes that can typically be attached to only one EC2 instance at a time (with exceptions for Multi-Attach). Option E (AWS Storage Gateway) is a hybrid cloud storage service, not a direct shared file system for EC2 instances.

text: Which Amazon S3 features can help manage data lifecycle and protect against accidental deletions? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Static website hosting","Versioning","Object-level access controls","Lifecycle policies","Cross-Region Replication"]
explanation: Option B (Versioning) helps protect against accidental deletions by keeping multiple versions of an object in the same S3 bucket, allowing for easy recovery. Option D (Lifecycle policies) allow you to define rules to automatically transition objects to different storage classes or delete them after a specified period, helping manage costs and data retention. Option A (Static website hosting) is a feature for hosting websites directly from S3, not for data protection or lifecycle management. Option C (Object-level access controls) manage who can access data, not accidental deletions or lifecycle. Option E (Cross-Region Replication) copies objects to another Region for disaster recovery, which is a form of data protection, but Versioning and Lifecycle policies are more direct for managing data within a single bucket's lifecycle and accidental deletions.

text: A company needs to transfer petabytes of data from its on-premises data center to AWS. The internet connection is slow and unreliable. Which AWS services are designed for large-scale offline data migration? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Storage Gateway","Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration","AWS Snowball","AWS Direct Connect","AWS Snowmobile"]
explanation: Option C (AWS Snowball) and Option E (AWS Snowmobile) are part of the AWS Snow Family, specifically designed for large-scale offline data migration. Snowball is a ruggedized device for transferring petabytes of data, while Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale data transfer service using a 45-foot shipping container. Option A (AWS Storage Gateway) is for hybrid cloud storage, not offline migration of petabytes. Option B (Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration) uses CloudFront edge locations to speed up transfers over the internet, but it's not for offline migration. Option D (AWS Direct Connect) provides a dedicated network connection, but it's still an online transfer method and might be too slow for petabytes of data with a poor internet connection.

text: Which AWS storage services provide block-level storage that can be attached to Amazon EC2 instances? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon S3","Amazon EBS","Amazon EFS","Instance Store","AWS Storage Gateway"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon EBS - Elastic Block Store) provides persistent block storage volumes for use with Amazon EC2 instances. These volumes behave like raw, unformatted block devices. Option D (Instance Store) provides temporary block-level storage for EC2 instances. Data on instance store volumes persists only for the life of the instance. Option A (Amazon S3) is object storage. Option C (Amazon EFS) is shared file storage. Option E (AWS Storage Gateway) is a hybrid cloud storage service, not direct block storage for EC2 instances.

text: Which AWS storage services provide highly durable object storage for a wide range of use cases, including static website hosting and backup? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EBS","Amazon S3","Amazon EFS","Amazon S3 Glacier","AWS Storage Gateway"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon S3 - Simple Storage Service) is an object storage service that offers industry-leading scalability, data availability, security, and performance, suitable for static website hosting, backup, and data archiving. Option D (Amazon S3 Glacier) is a low-cost storage service for data archiving and long-term backup, which is a specialized form of object storage. Option A (Amazon EBS) provides block storage for EC2 instances. Option C (Amazon EFS) provides shared file storage. Option E (AWS Storage Gateway) is a hybrid cloud storage service, not a primary object storage service itself.

text: Which AWS services are used for message queuing and decoupling components in a distributed application? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon SNS","Amazon SQS","AWS Lambda","Amazon EventBridge","Amazon Kinesis"]
explanation: Option A (Amazon SNS) is a fully managed messaging service for application-to-person (A2P) and application-to-application (A2A) communication, enabling fan-out messaging to multiple subscribers. Option B (Amazon SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service that enables you to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. Option C (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service. Option D (Amazon EventBridge) is a serverless event bus. Option E (Amazon Kinesis) is for real-time data streaming.

text: Which AWS services are designed to build event-driven architectures by routing events between various AWS services and your applications? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon SQS","Amazon SNS","Amazon EventBridge","AWS Step Functions","Amazon Kinesis"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon SNS) can publish messages to topics, which can then fan out to multiple subscribers, acting as an event source or target in an event-driven architecture. Option C (Amazon EventBridge) is a serverless event bus that makes it easier to connect applications together using data from your own applications, integrated SaaS applications, and AWS services. Option A (Amazon SQS) is a message queue for decoupling. Option D (AWS Step Functions) orchestrates workflows, not primarily for routing individual events. Option E (Amazon Kinesis) is for real-time data streaming.

text: A developer needs to orchestrate a series of serverless functions and microservices into a long-running, fault-tolerant workflow. Which AWS services can achieve this? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Lambda","AWS Step Functions","Amazon SQS","Amazon EventBridge","AWS CodePipeline"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Step Functions) is a serverless workflow service that orchestrates AWS Lambda functions and other AWS services into business-critical applications. Option D (Amazon EventBridge) can also be used to define rules that route events to targets, including Step Functions, to initiate and manage workflows. Option A (AWS Lambda) executes individual functions but does not orchestrate workflows. Option C (Amazon SQS) is a message queue for decoupling. Option E (AWS CodePipeline) is a continuous delivery service for automating release pipelines.

text: Which AWS services are primarily used to automate the release process for application updates, including building, testing, and deploying code? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Lambda","AWS CodePipeline","AWS CodeBuild","Amazon S3","Amazon EC2"]
explanation: Option B (AWS CodePipeline) is a continuous delivery service that automates your release pipelines for fast and reliable application and infrastructure updates. Option C (AWS CodeBuild) is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy. Option A (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service. Option D (Amazon S3) is object storage. Option E (Amazon EC2) provides virtual servers.

text: A company needs to decouple microservices using messaging and also send notifications to users based on application events. Which AWS services are suitable for these tasks? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Lambda","Amazon SQS","Amazon SNS","Amazon Kinesis","Amazon EventBridge"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service that enables you to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. Option C (Amazon SNS) is a fully managed messaging service for both application-to-application (A2A) and application-to-person (A2P) communication, making it ideal for sending notifications to users. Option A (AWS Lambda) is a compute service, not a messaging or notification service itself. Option D (Amazon Kinesis) is for real-time streaming data. Option E (Amazon EventBridge) is a serverless event bus that connects applications with data from various sources, but SQS and SNS are more direct for queuing and notifications.

text: Which AWS services can be used to coordinate multiple AWS Lambda functions and other services into serverless workflows? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon SQS","AWS Step Functions","Amazon SNS","Amazon EventBridge","AWS Glue"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Step Functions) is a serverless workflow service that lets you combine AWS Lambda functions and other AWS services to build business-critical applications. Option D (Amazon EventBridge) is a serverless event bus that makes it easier to connect applications together, routing events from various sources to targets like Lambda functions, enabling event-driven architectures and workflows. Option A (Amazon SQS) is a message queuing service for decoupling. Option C (Amazon SNS) is a notification service. Option E (AWS Glue) is an ETL service. While SQS and SNS can be part of workflows, Step Functions and EventBridge are specifically designed for orchestrating or routing events in workflows.

text: A company needs to build a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline for its application deployments. Which AWS services are specifically designed to automate the build, test, and deploy phases? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Lambda","AWS CodePipeline","Amazon S3","AWS CodeBuild","Amazon EC2"]
explanation: Option B (AWS CodePipeline) is a fully managed continuous delivery service that helps automate your release pipelines for fast and reliable application and infrastructure updates. Option D (AWS CodeBuild) is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy. Option A (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service, not directly a CI/CD tool. Option C (Amazon S3) can store artifacts but is not a CI/CD service itself. Option E (Amazon EC2) provides virtual servers, which can run CI/CD tools, but is not a managed CI/CD service.

text: Which AWS services are suitable for sending email notifications and managing email lists, or for sending push notifications to mobile devices? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon SQS","Amazon SNS","Amazon SES","AWS Lambda","Amazon EventBridge"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon SNS) is a highly available, durable, secure, fully managed pub/sub messaging service that enables you to send push notifications to mobile devices and email notifications. Option C (Amazon SES) is a flexible, scalable, and cost-effective email service that allows developers to send mail from within any application. Option A (Amazon SQS) is a message queuing service, not for direct user notifications. Option D (AWS Lambda) is a compute service that can be triggered by SNS or SES, but doesn't send notifications itself. Option E (Amazon EventBridge) is an event bus, which can route events that might trigger notifications, but is not the notification service itself.

text: A company wants to manage and connect IoT devices, and also needs a serverless platform for building and deploying web and mobile applications quickly. Which AWS services can fulfill these distinct requirements? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS IoT Core","AWS Lambda","AWS Amplify","Amazon EC2","Amazon S3"]
explanation: Option A (AWS IoT Core) is a managed cloud platform that lets connected devices easily and securely interact with cloud applications and other devices. Option C (AWS Amplify) is a complete solution that enables mobile and front-end web developers to build, ship, and host full-stack applications on AWS, including serverless backends. Option B (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service, which can be part of an Amplify backend or process IoT data, but it's not the primary service for IoT device management or full application development platform. Option D (Amazon EC2) provides virtual servers and is not serverless. Option E (Amazon S3) is object storage, not an IoT platform or application development platform.

text: Which AWS services are used for messaging and event-driven architectures? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon S3","Amazon SNS","Amazon SQS","AWS Lambda","Amazon CloudWatch"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon SNS - Simple Notification Service) is a fully managed messaging service for A2A (application-to-application) and A2P (application-to-person) communication, enabling fan-out capabilities. Option C (Amazon SQS - Simple Queue Service) is a fully managed message queuing service that enables you to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. Option A (Amazon S3) is object storage. Option D (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service, which can be triggered by messages but is not a messaging service itself. Option E (Amazon CloudWatch) is a monitoring and observability service.

text: A company wants to automate infrastructure provisioning and management using a declarative approach. Which AWS services support Infrastructure as Code (IaC)? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Management Console","AWS CloudFormation","AWS CLI","AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK)","AWS Elastic Beanstalk"]
explanation: Option B (AWS CloudFormation) and Option D (AWS Cloud Development Kit - CDK) are the primary AWS services for Infrastructure as Code (IaC). CloudFormation allows you to model and provision all your AWS resources using a declarative template. CDK allows you to define your cloud infrastructure using familiar programming languages. Option A (AWS Management Console) is a web-based UI for manual operations. Option C (AWS CLI) is a command-line tool for interacting with AWS services, but not an IaC tool for defining infrastructure. Option E (AWS Elastic Beanstalk) is a PaaS that deploys applications, but it's not a general IaC tool for all infrastructure.

text: A company wants to manage multiple AWS accounts centrally and apply common policies across them. Which AWS services are designed for this purpose? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS IAM","AWS Organizations","AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM)","AWS Control Tower","AWS SSO"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Organizations) helps you centrally manage and govern your environment as you grow and scale your AWS resources. It allows you to create a hierarchy of organizational units (OUs) and apply policies across accounts. Option D (AWS Control Tower) provides a way to set up and govern a secure, multi-account AWS environment, building on AWS Organizations. Option A (AWS IAM) manages users, groups, and roles within a single account. Option C (AWS Resource Access Manager - RAM) helps share AWS resources securely across AWS accounts, within your organization, or with other AWS accounts. Option E (AWS SSO) provides single sign-on access to multiple AWS accounts and business applications.

text: Which AWS services can be used to automate the deployment process for applications, enabling Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD)? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS CodeCommit","AWS CodePipeline","AWS CloudFormation","AWS CodeDeploy","AWS Lambda"]
explanation: Option B (AWS CodePipeline) is a fully managed continuous delivery service that helps automate your release pipelines for fast and reliable application and infrastructure updates. Option D (AWS CodeDeploy) automates code deployments to any instance, including Amazon EC2 instances and on-premises servers. Option A (AWS CodeCommit) is a source control service, which is a component of CI/CD but not the automation engine itself. Option C (AWS CloudFormation) is an Infrastructure as Code service, used to provision resources, which is part of CI/CD but not the deployment automation engine. Option E (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service, which can be used within a CI/CD pipeline but is not a CI/CD service itself.

text: Which of the following AWS pricing models offer significant discounts in exchange for a commitment to a 1-year or 3-year term? (Select TWO.)
options: ["On-Demand pricing","Reserved Instances","Spot Instances","AWS Free Tier","Savings Plans"]
explanation: Option B (Reserved Instances) and Option E (Savings Plans) are both pricing models that provide significant discounts (up to 72%) in exchange for a commitment to a 1-year or 3-year term. Option A (On-Demand pricing) offers flexibility with no commitment but is the most expensive. Option C (Spot Instances) offers deep discounts for interruptible workloads without a long-term commitment. Option D (AWS Free Tier) provides limited free usage for new accounts, not long-term commitment discounts for steady-state workloads.

text: Which two characteristics accurately describe AWS Spot Instances? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Ideal for steady-state production workloads","Can be interrupted by AWS with two minutes of notice","Offer up to 90% savings compared to On-Demand pricing","Require a 1-year commitment for usage","Provide dedicated compute capacity for critical applications"]
explanation: Option B (Can be interrupted by AWS with two minutes of notice) and Option C (Offer up to 90% savings compared to On-Demand pricing) are key characteristics of AWS Spot Instances. Spot Instances leverage unused EC2 capacity, making them highly cost-effective but interruptible. Option A (Ideal for steady-state production workloads) is incorrect; Reserved Instances or Savings Plans are better for steady-state workloads. Option D (Require a 1-year commitment for usage) is incorrect, as Spot Instances are typically used for short-term, flexible compute. Option E (Provide dedicated compute capacity for critical applications) is incorrect, as Spot Instances are not suitable for critical, uninterrupted workloads.

text: Which of the following are benefits provided by the AWS Free Tier? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Provides unlimited usage for all AWS services","Allows new AWS customers to explore services at no cost","Includes offers that are always free or free for 12 months","Offers a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM)","Guarantees 99.99% uptime for free resources"]
explanation: Option B (Allows new AWS customers to explore services at no cost) and Option C (Includes offers that are always free or free for 12 months) correctly describe benefits of the AWS Free Tier. The Free Tier enables users to experiment with AWS services without incurring charges for a limited scope. Option A (Provides unlimited usage for all AWS services) is incorrect; the Free Tier has specific usage limits. Option D (Offers a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM)) is incorrect; TAMs are only available with Enterprise On-Ramp and Enterprise Support plans. Option E (Guarantees 99.99% uptime for free resources) is incorrect; the Free Tier does not provide specific uptime guarantees beyond standard service SLAs.

text: Regarding data transfer costs within AWS, which statements are generally true? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Data transfer inbound to AWS from the internet is typically free","Data transfer between Availability Zones in the same Region is always free","Data transfer out of AWS to the internet is charged","All data transfer within the same AWS Region is free","Data transfer between AWS Regions is always free"]
explanation: Option A (Data transfer inbound to AWS from the internet is typically free) is correct, as AWS generally does not charge for data coming into its network. Option C (Data transfer out of AWS to the internet is charged) is also correct, as outbound data transfer is a common cost component. Option B (Data transfer between Availability Zones in the same Region is always free) is incorrect; there is typically a charge for data transfer between Availability Zones. Option D (All data transfer within the same AWS Region is free) is incorrect due to inter-AZ transfer costs. Option E (Data transfer between AWS Regions is always free) is incorrect; cross-Region data transfer is always charged.

text: Which two statements correctly describe the characteristics of On-Demand pricing for AWS services like Amazon EC2? (Select TWO.)
options: ["It provides the lowest cost option for steady-state workloads.","You pay for compute capacity by the second or hour with no long-term commitment.","It requires a 1-year or 3-year commitment.","It offers flexibility for unpredictable workloads.","Instances can be interrupted by AWS with short notice."]
explanation: Option B (You pay for compute capacity by the second or hour with no long-term commitment) and Option D (It offers flexibility for unpredictable workloads) accurately describe On-Demand pricing. This model is ideal for workloads with fluctuating demand or for initial development. Option A (It provides the lowest cost option for steady-state workloads) is incorrect; Reserved Instances or Savings Plans offer lower costs for predictable usage. Option C (It requires a 1-year or 3-year commitment) is incorrect, as this applies to Reserved Instances and Savings Plans. Option E (Instances can be interrupted by AWS with short notice) is incorrect; this is a characteristic of Spot Instances, not On-Demand instances.

text: A company is planning to migrate several steady-state, long-running applications to AWS. They want to minimize costs for their Amazon EC2 instances by committing to a specific usage term. Which EC2 pricing models should they consider to achieve significant discounts? (Select TWO.)
options: ["On-Demand Instances","Reserved Instances","Spot Instances","Dedicated Hosts","Savings Plans"]
explanation: Option B (Reserved Instances) and Option E (Savings Plans) are designed for workloads with predictable, steady-state usage, offering significant discounts (up to 72%) in exchange for a 1-year or 3-year commitment. Option A (On-Demand Instances) is the most expensive option and provides flexibility without commitment, making it unsuitable for cost optimization of steady-state workloads. Option C (Spot Instances) offers even deeper discounts but is suitable only for fault-tolerant, interruptible workloads, not typically steady-state applications. Option D (Dedicated Hosts) provides dedicated physical servers for regulatory compliance or licensing requirements, which is not primarily a cost-saving pricing model for general steady-state applications.

text: Which of the following statements accurately describe how data transfer is typically priced within AWS? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Data transfer out from AWS to the internet is generally free.","Data transfer into AWS from the internet is generally free.","Data transfer between different AWS Regions is always free.","Data transfer between Availability Zones within the same AWS Region is generally free.","Data transfer between Availability Zones within the same AWS Region is charged."]
explanation: Option B (Data transfer into AWS from the internet is generally free) is correct; inbound data transfer to AWS is typically free across most services. Option E (Data transfer between Availability Zones within the same AWS Region is charged) is correct; while data transfer within the same Availability Zone is free, moving data between different Availability Zones within the same Region incurs a charge. Option A (Data transfer out from AWS to the internet is generally free) is incorrect; outbound data transfer from AWS to the internet is charged. Option C (Data transfer between different AWS Regions is always free) is incorrect; data transfer between different AWS Regions is always charged. Option D (Data transfer between Availability Zones within the same AWS Region is generally free) is incorrect, as explained for Option E.

text: A media company needs to process large volumes of video files for transcoding. These jobs can be interrupted and resumed later without significant impact. The company's primary goal is to minimize compute costs for this workload. Which EC2 pricing models should they consider? (Select TWO.)
options: ["On-Demand Instances","Reserved Instances","Spot Instances","Dedicated Hosts","EC2 Savings Plans"]
explanation: Option C (Spot Instances) is ideal for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads like video transcoding, offering up to 90% savings compared to On-Demand pricing, as these instances can be interrupted. Option E (EC2 Savings Plans) also provides significant discounts (up to 66%) for a commitment to compute usage, which can include EC2 instances, and offers flexibility across instance families, sizes, and Regions, making it suitable for long-term cost reduction. Option A (On-Demand Instances) is the most expensive and offers no cost savings for this type of workload. Option B (Reserved Instances) requires a commitment to a specific instance type and Region, which is less flexible than Savings Plans and not ideal for interruptible workloads that might change instance types. Option D (Dedicated Hosts) is for specific licensing or compliance needs and is not a cost-optimization strategy for general batch processing.

text: A new startup is exploring AWS services for their application development and wants to keep initial costs as low as possible. Which of the following are benefits offered by the AWS Free Tier? (Select TWO.)
options: ["A fixed monthly credit for all AWS services for the first year.","Access to a limited number of services that are always free, regardless of account age.","A 12-month free period for certain services, allowing usage up to specific limits.","Unlimited usage of all AWS services for the first 30 days.","Automatic application of the deepest discounts available for Reserved Instances."]
explanation: Option B (Access to a limited number of services that are always free, regardless of account age) is correct, as some services like AWS Lambda (1 million free requests per month) and Amazon DynamoDB (25 GB storage, 25 million read/write units) offer an 'Always Free' tier. Option C (A 12-month free period for certain services, allowing usage up to specific limits) is also correct, as many popular services like Amazon EC2 (750 hours/month of t2.micro or t3.micro) and Amazon S3 (5 GB of Standard Storage) provide a 12-month free tier for new accounts.
